feed.title: American Assets Trust Executive Chairman Rady Buys Over $1 Million Shares. Does This Make AAT a Buy?
feed.summary: Ernest S. Rady, Executive Chairman of American Assets Trust (AAT), purchased 50,000 shares of common stock for approximately $1.1 million on September 14, 2026, increasing his total holdings to about 14.4 million shares. This insider buying signals a strong bullish sentiment, especially considering his previous significant purchases, as insiders typically buy shares only when they expect the price to rise. The company, a REIT specializing in premium office, retail, and residential properties, is showing strength in its business with robust multifamily rents and strong tourism at its Hawaii hotel properties.

feed.title: Keurig Dr Pepper Beat PepsiCo Over the Past Year. Income Investors May See It Differently
feed.summary: While Keurig Dr Pepper's stock has outperformed PepsiCo's in the past year, income investors seeking dividend stability may find PepsiCo to be the better choice. PepsiCo offers a higher yield, consistent free cash flow coverage, and a 54-year dividend raise track record, alongside a diversified snack and beverage business. In contrast, Keurig Dr Pepper's dividend has stalled, it carries significant debt, and an upcoming company split could impact dividend continuity.

feed.title: US jury says Apple owes record $5.7 billion in haptic technology patent case
feed.summary: A US jury has ordered Apple to pay San Diego-based Taction over $5.7 billion for infringing two of its patents related to haptic feedback technology used in iPhones and Apple Watches. Apple disputes the verdict, stating its Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction's technology, and plans to appeal what is reportedly the largest such verdict to date. Taction, which applies its technology in headphones and gaming headsets, initiated the lawsuit in 2021, a case revived by a federal appeals court after an initial ruling favored Apple.

feed.title: Oracle vs. Alphabet: Which AI Cloud Stock Is the Better Buy?
feed.summary: This article compares Oracle and Alphabet as AI cloud stocks, highlighting their differing financial models and risks. Oracle shows faster cloud growth but faces significant financing challenges due to capital intensity, while Alphabet, despite its broad revenue streams, is also incurring substantial capital expenditures for its AI build. The author concludes that while Oracle offers higher rerating upside for those willing to accept financing risk, Alphabet is the stronger risk-adjusted choice due to its more profitable business segments funding its AI growth.

feed.title: Anthropic Needs Gigawatts of Power It Doesn't Have. This Dividend-Paying Industrial Sells It.
feed.summary: NextEra Energy (NYSE: NEE) is presented as a strong solution for the massive power demands of AI data centers, including those of Anthropic. The company's Energy Resources subsidiary offers diverse power solutions, including renewables, natural gas, battery storage, and nuclear power, and is actively expanding its capacity with a 35 GW project backlog. Investors can benefit from NextEra's growth potential and a projected 10% dividend increase this year, with annual growth targeted through 2028.

feed.title: Own 141 Shares of Chevron (CVX) and Collect $1,000 a Year in Dividends
feed.summary: This article discusses how owning 141 shares of Chevron (CVX) can generate $1,000 in annual dividend income, based on its current forward annualized dividend of $7.12 per share. It highlights Chevron's 39-year dividend growth streak, robust cash flow, and strong balance sheet, which support its dividend even as the stock trades near its 52-week high. The author advises potential investors to consider the entry yield at the current price and model for potential dividend cuts due to Chevron's oil-linked earnings.

feed.title: Financials slump amid sector rotation into technology; Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley in week's losers
feed.summary: Wall Street saw a significant sector rotation from financials into technology, driven by increased AI spending and capital markets activity. The State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) rose while the State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF (XLF) declined, partly due to fears of AI disruption from Meta's Muse. Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley were among the biggest financial losers, while Citigroup saw gains, and several mid-cap and small-cap financial firms experienced notable shifts.

feed.title: Financials slump amid sector rotation into technology; Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley in week's losers
feed.summary: The financial sector experienced a slump this week as market activity shifted towards technology, driven by significant AI-related spending. This sector rotation led to underperformance for financial stocks, with Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley identified among the week's biggest losers. Concerns over AI-driven disruption and company-specific events contributed to the decline in bank, insurer, and payment stocks.

feed.title: ISS backs two ATG nominees for Empery Digital board
feed.summary: Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) has recommended that Empery Digital Inc. stockholders vote for two board nominees proposed by activist investor ATG Capital Management LP at the upcoming October 14 annual meeting. ISS also advised shareholders to withhold support from two incumbent directors and vote against the company’s equity incentive plan, aligning with ATG Capital's efforts to appoint four candidates to the board. This recommendation follows a Delaware Chancery Court finding that Empery Digital’s board improperly invalidated ATG Capital’s director nominations.

feed.summary: Masonglory, INLIF, and Apimeds experienced significant stock surges driven by strategic acquisitions, strong financial results, and new service agreements, respectively. Masonglory's shares rose over 300% after a share swap deal, INLIF gained about 74% due to improved first-half results, and Apimeds Pharmaceuticals increased over 47% after a subsidiary secured a technology services contract. These gains were supported by unusually high trading volumes, reflecting strong investor confidence.

feed.title: Sarepta Therapeutics (SRPT) Falls As Patent Settlement Tests The Undervalued Narrative
feed.summary: Sarepta Therapeutics (SRPT) experienced a 7.1% share price drop following a sector-wide biotech selloff and a major patent litigation settlement, pushing its stock to $18.39. Analysts currently value SRPT at $21.65, suggesting it is 15% undervalued, but its future depends on pipeline development and resolution of gene therapy safety concerns and administrative delays.

feed.title: McDonald’s Sell-Off Hits 30% as Big Mac Inflation Spurs Pushback
feed.summary: McDonald's stock has fallen nearly 31% from its February high, heading for its worst annual return since 2002, as customers push back against rising menu prices and a perceived decline in value. The company's recent investor day indicated "slightly negative" US sales for the current quarter, prompting concerns about its strategy to reinvigorate sales through technology investments, restaurant upgrades, and market share gains in chicken and beverages. Despite these challenges, Wall Street analysts largely maintain positive ratings, with an average price target suggesting a 28% return.

feed.title: T-Mobile US (NASDAQ:TMUS) Stock Price Target Lowered at The Goldman Sachs Group
feed.summary: The Goldman Sachs Group has lowered its price target for T-Mobile US (NASDAQ:TMUS) from $230 to $211, while maintaining a "Buy" rating, projecting a potential upside of 27.55% from its previous close. Despite this reduction and other recent target cuts from various firms, the consensus analyst rating remains a "Moderate Buy" with an average price target of $249.48. T-Mobile recently surpassed earnings expectations, reporting $2.99 EPS against a $2.59 consensus, and saw a 7.9% year-over-year revenue increase to $22.79 billion.

feed.title: NextEra Energy Backlog Reaches 35.1 GW as It Targets Data-Center Demand
feed.summary: NextEra Energy's project backlog has grown to approximately 35.1 GW, driven by significant additions of solar, battery storage, and wind projects in Q2 2026. The company is actively pursuing opportunities to serve large electricity users, particularly data centers, with targets of securing 15 GW to 30 GW of new generation by 2035. Its utility subsidiary, Florida Power & Light, also reports substantial interest from large-load customers, indicating a strong future demand for NextEra's diversified energy portfolio.

feed.title: Titan International signs definitive agreement to sell ITM undercarriage business to Schlam owner USCO SpA
feed.summary: Titan International Inc. has announced a definitive agreement to sell its Italtractor ITM undercarriage business (ITM) to USCO SpA for an initial purchase price of US$207 million, with potential for an additional US$6 million in earnout proceeds. The transaction, expected to close in early January 2027, will allow Titan to focus on its core global wheel and tyre operations. USCO SpA aims to consolidate its leading position in construction and expand its mining sector presence through this acquisition.

feed.title: S&P Global Calls AM General’s Outlook Negative, Lowers Credit Rating
feed.summary: S&P Global has downgraded AM General's credit rating from B- to CCC and issued a negative outlook due to underperforming JLTV A2 production, significant financial leverage, and concerns over refinancing looming maturities. While the company has a robust backlog, production delays and changes in executive management have contributed to the downgrade, raising uncertainty despite projected revenue growth in 2026 and 2027.

feed.title: CarMax Stock Forecast: Used-Car Demand Faces Major Q2 Earnings Test
feed.summary: CarMax (KMX) is set to release its Q2 earnings, with analysts anticipating revenue of $6.97 billion and EPS of $0.72. The company faces challenges with soft retail demand and declining gross profit per vehicle, despite increased wholesale volume and cost-cutting efforts. Investors will be scrutinizing retail unit recovery, financing performance from CarMax Auto Finance, and profit margins to gauge sustainable growth.

feed.title: Dollar General CEO warns $100k a year is no longer enough to feel like you’re higher income
feed.summary: Dollar General's CEO, Todd Vasos, notes that customers across all income levels, including those earning over $100,000 annually, are experiencing financial distress due to inflation. He states that even high-income earners no longer feel like they are making enough. Research supports this, showing that many high-income households are struggling with debt and living paycheck to paycheck, underscoring the broad impact of sustained price increases.

feed.title: Verizon Stock Is 8% Off Its September Peak. Here’s the Q3 Test Its CEO Set
feed.summary: Verizon's stock has dropped 8.49% from its mid-September peak, closing at $47.08 on September 25, though it remains up 15.6% for 2026. This decline followed the Federal Reserve's first rate hike since 2023 and other factors like T-Mobile's account growth guidance and an FAA system outage. CEO Dan Schulman has set a key Q3 test focusing on positive phone net accounts and growing per-customer revenue, guiding for 2026 postpaid phone net additions in the upper half of 750,000 to 1 million.

feed.title: Coca-Cola poaches Monster Energy executive to lead U.S. and Canada operations as $2.6 billion African bottling deal moves closer to completion
feed.summary: Coca-Cola has appointed Rob Gehring, former head of Monster Beverage's Americas business, to lead its North America unit starting December 1st. This leadership change occurs as Coca-Cola HBC AG, the company's bottling partner, is nearing completion of a $2.55 billion acquisition of a 75% controlling interest in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa, with regulatory approvals progressing across various African jurisdictions. The transitions happen amidst shifting consumer behavior and economic pressures, though both Monster Beverage and Coca-Cola HBC have reported strong sales.

feed.title: Best Buy Is Turning Amazon Fire TV Into a New Advertising Opportunity
feed.summary: Best Buy is expanding its business model beyond traditional electronics retail by developing a high-margin advertising platform, notably through an expanded partnership with Amazon Fire TV. This initiative, set to launch in February 2027, will leverage Best Buy's customer data for programmatic advertising on connected televisions, turning hardware sales into recurring revenue. Despite some analyst skepticism and insider selling, the company's core retail business is stabilizing, and its advertising revenue, projected to approach $1 billion annually, is expected to significantly boost profitability and expand margins.

feed.title: At least 3 Starbucks on Long Island among 250 to be closed in latest round of shutdowns
feed.summary: Starbucks is closing approximately 250 North American stores, including at least three on Long Island, as part of a turnaround strategy. These closures represent about 1% of the company's North American shops and are primarily underperforming locations. The company aims to reestablish its position as a community coffeehouse by enhancing in-store experiences and remodeling existing stores, while employees from closed stores will have transfer or severance options.

feed.title: Monster Beverage (MNST) CEO Americas Rob Gehring to Resign, Emel
feed.summary: Monster Beverage (MNST) announced that Rob Gehring, CEO Americas, will resign on November 30, 2026, to return to The Coca-Cola Company as president of its North America operating unit. Emelie C. Tirre, currently Chief Strategy Officer, will assume interim leadership for the Americas and Caribbean starting December 1, 2026. The company has not yet named a permanent replacement for the position.

feed.title: Acadia Pharmaceuticals Announces Phase 3 Enabling Topline Results from Phase 2 RADIANT Study of Remlifanserin for the Treatment of Alzheimer’s Disease Psychosis (ADP)
feed.summary: Acadia Pharmaceuticals announced positive Phase 2 results for remlifanserin in Alzheimer's Disease Psychosis (ADP), showing a significant reduction in hallucinations and delusions with the 60 mg dose, and a favorable safety profile. The company plans to continue its Phase 3 program, removing the 30 mg dose arm, and will present detailed findings at the CTAD conference. Remlifanserin is a novel 5HT2A receptor inverse agonist with no FDA-approved treatment currently available for ADP, addressing a high unmet medical need.

feed.title: Larry Ellison adds $9.2 billion in Oracle shares as loan collateral
feed.summary: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison has pledged an additional 67 million Oracle shares, valued at approximately $9.2 billion, as collateral for personal loans, increasing his pledged stock by 19% since 2025. This move aligns with his financing efforts for his son David Ellison’s Paramount Skydance acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. Despite Oracle's policy against pledging shares for officers and directors, Ellison, as executive chair and CTO, is exempt.

feed.title: How Dental Financing Integration Will Impact Synchrony Financial (SYF) Investors
feed.summary: Synchrony Financial (SYF) is partnering with Intelibly Inc. to embed its CareCredit health and wellness credit card into Intelibly’s dental appointment platform, providing patients with financing options earlier in their care journey. This integration aligns with Synchrony's broader strategy of embedded finance, as seen with Amazon, Walmart, and PayPal, and is viewed as another test of this approach. While it is not expected to immediately transform the short-term earnings outlook, it could shift more dental spending towards Synchrony Financial's health and wellness vertical.

feed.title: Bambu Lab Paying Out $27.6M In Massive 3D Printer Tech Lawsuit
feed.summary: Bambu Lab, a major 3D printer company, has been ordered to pay Stratasys, Ltd. over $27 million in damages for patent infringement in a Texas lawsuit. The lawsuit concerned technologies like automatic bed leveling and purge towers, primarily affecting Bambu Lab's first-generation products. Despite a similar suit in Europe ruling in Bambu Lab's favor, the company plans to appeal the U.S. verdict, though existing printers are not expected to be affected, and newer models use different technology.

feed.title: If You Invest $100 Per Month in Procter & Gamble Stock, Here's the Passive Dividend Income It Could Generate Over 10 Years
feed.summary: This article examines the passive dividend income an investor could generate by investing $100 per month in Procter & Gamble (NYSE: PG) stock over 10 years. It highlights that P&G, a consumer staples company, currently offers a dividend yield of nearly 3% and has consistently raised its dividend for 70 consecutive years. While a rough calculation suggests $1,951 in cumulative income over a decade from a $12,000 investment, the article notes this estimate doesn't fully account for dividend increases and stock price appreciation, both of which could significantly boost actual returns.
